brief: Bad vs Good vs Great prompts — what changes as you climb each tier.

slots.body: Bad prompts force the model to guess your intent. Good prompts state the task clearly. Great prompts frame the strategic outcome before a single word is written.
slots.note: Write the last sentence first, then work backward.

slots.body: Good prompts include basic background. Great prompts supply audience, constraints, prior failures, and success metrics in one breath.
slots.note: Treat context as a briefing, not an afterthought.

slots.body: Bad prompts accept a wall of text. Great prompts define headers, tone, length, and even the exact markdown structure needed.
slots.note: Paste a template into the prompt if you have one.

slots.body: Good prompts ask for an expert. Great prompts define the persona’s biases, communication style, and the reader they are speaking to.
slots.note: The more specific the persona, the sharper the output.

slots.body: Bad prompts demand an answer immediately. Great prompts instruct the model to think aloud, check assumptions, and cite sources before concluding.
slots.note: Add 'Explain your reasoning before you answer' for instant gains.

slots.body: Good prompts are written once. Great prompts ask the model to score its own draft against your criteria and revise accordingly.
slots.note: Turn one prompt into a feedback loop, not a single shot.

slots.body: Start with one tier jump today, and watch the output transform before your eyes.
